rule_changes.title: No SG Arrival Card without a valid Singapore VEP
rule_changes.body: Since 6 October 2026, nobody travelling in a foreign-registered car can submit the SG Arrival Card unless the car already holds a valid Singapore Vehicle Entry Permit from LTA. That includes every passenger. The permit needs Singapore motor insurance, so sort both before the trip.

rule_changes.title: Motorcycles can use automated car lanes leaving Woodlands
rule_changes.body: Since 15 October 2026, motorcyclists and pillion riders leaving Singapore through Woodlands can clear immigration by face recognition at selected departure car lanes.

rule_changes.title: Unpaid Singapore fines block the VEP and entry
rule_changes.body: From 2 November 2026, a foreign-registered car, motorcycle, taxi, bus or goods vehicle with unpaid Singapore traffic, parking or emissions fines cannot apply for or renew its VEP, and ICA will refuse it entry at Woodlands and Tuas.
rule_changes.source_name: LTA and MHA joint release, 15 May 2026

rule_changes.title: More cross-border taxis, two more booking apps
rule_changes.body: From 16 November 2026, the cross-border taxi scheme grows from 300 to 500 licensed taxis per country, and CDG Zig and Kumpool join Grab as licensed booking platforms.

rule_changes.title: Jalan Jim Quee beside the JB checkpoint closes to private cars
rule_changes.body: Johor's transport councillor says the road beside the Johor Bahru checkpoint will take only buses and taxis from 20 December 2026, with e-hailing pick-ups moved to Jalan Tun Razak. No official notice yet, and the same paper reported 2027 in September, so check before relying on it.

rule_changes.title: Last day for the cheaper ERP2 unit for foreign cars
rule_changes.body: Foreign-registered vehicles can buy Singapore's ERP2 on-board unit at S$158.70 until 31 December 2026. The unit is optional, but without one a vehicle pays a flat road-pricing fee from 2027.

rule_changes.title: Singapore VEP rises to S$50 a day, free days end
rule_changes.body: From 1 January 2027, the VEP for foreign cars rises from S$35 to S$50 a day and for motorcycles from S$4 to S$7. It still does not apply on weekends and Singapore public holidays, but the 10 free days a year and the free weekday hours end. A vehicle without an ERP2 unit pays a flat S$10 (motorcycles S$3) on each day road pricing runs. The goods vehicle permit rises from S$40 to S$70 a month.

rule_changes.title: Malaysian taxis pay S$15 a trip into Singapore
rule_changes.body: From 1 January 2027, the permit for a Malaysia-registered taxi entering Singapore changes from S$2 a month to S$15 a trip. Expect cross-border fares to rise.

rule_changes.title: RTS Link opening targeted for February 2027
rule_changes.body: The operator has told both governments that the Johor Bahru to Woodlands North rail link should open in February 2027, later than the earlier end-2026 target, subject to independent safety certification and final approval. No exact date yet, and fares are due by the end of 2026. Five minutes station to station, up to 10,000 passengers an hour each way, immigration for both countries cleared at the departure station.
rule_changes.source_name: LTA and Malaysia MOT joint release, 2 Oct 2026

standing_rules.title: Johor's weekend is Saturday and Sunday
standing_rules.body: Johor moved its rest days back to Saturday and Sunday on 1 January 2025, so both sides of the Causeway now share the same weekend.

standing_rules.title: Malaysia enforces its own VEP on Singapore cars
standing_rules.body: Singapore-registered vehicles need a Malaysian VEP tag to enter Johor. Enforcement began in phases from 1 October 2024.

standing_rules.title: Leave Singapore with three-quarters of a tank
standing_rules.body: Singapore-registered cars leaving through Woodlands or Tuas must carry at least three-quarters of a tank of fuel. Singapore Customs enforces it, with fines of up to S$500.

standing_rules.title: Live traffic by phone
standing_rules.body: ICA's CHECK-TIPS hotline for the checkpoint traffic situation is 6863 0117.

single_day.note: Record single-day crossings at Woodlands and Tuas combined, beating 598,000 on 19 June 2026.
